# The Promise in the Sky's Turning

## Scripture

*"While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall not cease."* — Genesis 8:22 (ESV)

## Reflection

As September settles in, the night sky itself seems to turn a page. The Summer Triangle—Vega, Deneb, and Altair—still hangs overhead after dusk, but it's drifting westward now. Pegasus rises in the east, and before long, Orion will return to the predawn hours. The heavens are quietly shifting, announcing that fall is near.

We often treat change as something to dread. But look at what God attached to this promise, spoken to Noah after the flood: the turning of seasons is a covenant of faithfulness. Every year, without fail, the sky rotates and the air cools. God didn't promise a world without change—He promised a world where change itself testifies to His steady character.

Maybe you're in a season of transition right now—a new job, a shifting friendship, a chapter closing. The autumn sky preaches a gentle sermon: turning is not abandonment. The God who tilts the earth on its axis and rolls the constellations across the dark is the same God who holds your changing life. Seedtime and harvest still come. Day and night still keep their appointment. And so does His love.

## Prayer

Father, thank You that even as the seasons turn, Your faithfulness never does. When my life feels like shifting skies, anchor me in Your unchanging character. Help me trust the One who set the stars in motion and holds my days in His hands. Amen.

---

**Observation for tonight:** Look for the Great Square of Pegasus rising in the eastern sky after sunset—a signpost of autumn's arrival and a reminder that God's promises, like the seasons, always come around again.
